messages:
Maya: Heads-up: noticed a +170ms jump in p95 for /v1/generate (prod-us-west) right after we changed the routing policy. No infra deploy. Screenshot: https://console.redwood/trace.png Any chance this is just an aggregation artifact?
Rafael: Opening quick check. We do endpoint rollups by combining per-route sketches into one summary. A reweighting of samples can move the endpoint percentiles even when individual route latencies stayed flat.
Sam: This is the classic sample-composition problem. Our alerting currently watches endpoint p95 which made the oncall noisy during the rollout. We should either (A) expose route-attributed percentiles or (B) provide an aggregation-mode knob so callers can pick conservative semantics.
Nina: UX idea: add a tiny "source breakdown" pill next to the pctl with counts, e.g., "sources: dedicated 58% | hosted 42%" and a chevron to expand into a per-route chart. Also add a short inline note: "Rollup shown uses 'sketch-merge' aggregation; changes to routing or quota may shift values."
Maya: Love the pill. On alerting side—we could recommend binding SLOs to route-level metrics or to a conservative rollup mode that returns the max per-route pctl so SREs don't get paged for weight-only changes.
metrics-bot: metric-alert: p95 threshold exceeded for /v1/generate (prod-us-west) at 2025-04-02T11:12:07Z.
Rafael: API proposal: add `rollup_mode` param to metrics API with values `sketch-merge`(current), `route-weighted`, `route-max`. Also add `include_sources=true` to return per-route sample counts and a small histogram of sample sizes. That avoids breaking existing clients.
Sam: For alerting best practices, I'll update the runbook: prefer `route` SLOs when routes differ in capacity; otherwise use `rollup_mode=route-max` for conservative alarms. I'll also add a test that flips routing weights and asserts that alerts don't fire when route-level latencies are stable.
Nina: I'll prototype the UI pill + expand view. Copy suggestion: "Aggregated across routes. Use breakdown to inspect route-level percentiles or switch rollup mode for conservative alerts."
Maya: Action owners: Maya -> update incident note + oncall guidance; Rafael -> RFC & API impl; Sam -> runbook + tests; Nina -> UI pill + docs link. Can we ship UI canary + API flag behind a feature toggle in the next deploy?
Rafael: Yes. I'll include API compatibility examples in the RFC and a small swagger snippet: ```GET /metrics?metric=latency_percentile&endpoint=/v1/generate&percentile=95&rollup_mode=route-weighted&include_sources=true```
Sam: Also add an opt-in telemetry tag on request events when quota reroutes happen: `reroute.trigger=quota` so the console can annotate the timeline and help correlate pctl shifts with quota activity.
metrics-bot: note: historical p95 trend annotated at 2025-04-02T10:50:00Z with event: quota.reroute for hosted->dedicated.
deploy-bot: scheduled deploy: console-source-pill-canary -> 2025-04-03T02:00:00Z (includes UI pill behind flag).
Maya: Thanks. If we make the conservative rollup available and surface source counts by default, we should cut down noise and make percentiles less surprising during rollouts.
Rafael: Opening the RFC now. Will @ everyone in #pr-links when it's up.
